figures.finding: Saudi Arabia levies no income tax on an individual's earnings from employment; non-employment (business) income is taxed as an entity or permanent establishment, and a resident non-Saudi doing temporary work outside employment is taxed at 20%.

value.businessIncome: taxed as entity/PE (20% for non-Saudi residents)

sources.said: There is no individual income tax scheme in Saudi Arabia. Income tax is not imposed on an individual's earnings if they are derived only from employment in Saudi Arabia. Non-employment income is taxed as an entity or permanent establishment (PE).

Yes, amounts earned by visiting expatriates performing temporary work in the Kingdom are subject to income tax at 20% or Tax Withholding at 15%, depending on their residency status, unless such amounts arise from an employment relationship governed by applicable labor laws with all employment conditions met.

figures.finding: Nothing is withheld from employment pay for tax, since none is levied.

sources.said: There is no individual income tax scheme in Saudi Arabia.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer, writer or director paid by a Saudi resident for work done in the Kingdom (not as an employee) bears withholding: 15% on 'any other payments' and on royalties, 5% on technical and consulting services, 20% on management fees; it is paid by the 10th of the next month.

value.due: first ten days of the following month

figures.applies: Payments from a resident or PE to a non-resident without a PE, 2026; treaties may reduce royalties.

figures.finding: Payments for the right to use a literary, artistic or film work protected by copyright are royalties, withheld at 15% when paid to a non-resident.

figures.finding: Contributions are on monthly basic salary plus housing up to SAR 45,000: a Saudi employee pays 9.75% (9% pension, 0.75% SANED) and the employer 11.75% (adding 2% occupational hazard); for a non-Saudi only the employer's 2% occupational hazard applies.
figures.applies: 2026 (rates for new Saudi entrants under the 2024 Social Insurance Law were not read here).

sources.said: Social insurance contributions are paid monthly based on the monthly basic salary plus housing (paid or in kind) with an upper limit of SAR 45,000, are computed at 2% for non-Saudi employees (note that this is not social insurance, it is occupational hazard), and are paid by the employer. For Saudi employees, the rate is 21.5% and is paid by both the employee (9.75% = 9% social insurance + 0.75% unemployment insurance [SANED]) and the employer (11.75% = 9% social insurance + 2% occupational hazard + 0.75% unemployment insurance [SANED]).

figures.finding: VAT is 15% since 1 July 2020; a resident must register within 30 days of a month-end at which his past twelve months' supplies (or the next twelve months' expected) exceed the Mandatory Registration Threshold the GCC Agreement sets (its amount not read).

sources.said: Effective 1 July 2020, the standard VAT rate was increased by the government to 15%.

every Resident Person in the Kingdom who is not registered by the Authority must at the end of each month calculate the value of his Supplies made in the Kingdom within the twelve months then ended, in accordance with the requirements set out in the Agreement. In cases where this value exceeds the Mandatory Registration Threshold detailed in the Agreement, the Person must apply to the Authority to register within thirty (30) days of the end of that month
